solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way that saves time for Bob, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a quicker route than the usual one
a bob is a hairstyle that is trimmed close, an example of a brief haircut

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a quick route that suits a man called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' reads as a man's name, but it is the hairstyle; 'for' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a quicker route, and a haircut that is not long, of which a bob is one example.

clue.text: Peel off football kit

definitions.meaning: to remove a layer or clothing
a team's playing outfit in British usage

explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to peel off a layer; in Britain a team's playing kit is also called its strip.

clue.text: Moorland oppressively hems in US city

indicators.note: hems in means the words surround and conceal the city's name

explanation.surface: Bleak moorland heavily encloses an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hems in' hides the answer in moORLAND Oppressively.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in Florida, famous for its theme parks.

clue.text: Pills protecting nine playing sport

indicators.note: protecting means the pills' synonym wraps round the other letters

parts.note: tablets are pills

indicators.note: playing means the letters of nine are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nine people on medication take part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' (shuffling ENNI) suggests the sport itself; it is the anagram signal, and 'protecting' means the pills wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong, played with bats across a net on a table, is an indoor sport.

clue.text: University's head of equality: 'Vote for men and women'

parts.note: uni is short for university, plus the 's

indicators.note: head of means just the first letter of the word equality

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A university's equality chief issues a slogan urging a vote for all genders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes E from equality; X is the cross on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex describes clothing or facilities designed to suit both sexes alike.

clue.text: Go around on southern motorway creating air pollution

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word go back to front

explanation.surface: A driver circles round on a motorway in the south, adding to the haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the turnaround signal; 'on' means placed after, as in an across clue one piece follows another.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a thick haze of smoke and fog, a familiar kind of dirty air.

clue.text: Mode of speech in grand house

indicators.note: of speech means the word is as heard when spoken

parts.note: a manner is a mode or way of doing something

explanation.surface: Describing how people talk in a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mode of speech' looks like one phrase for accent; 'of speech' is in fact the sound signal on MANNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with lands, historically a lord's estate.

clue.text: Wrestle with pages in large spread

indicators.note: in means the pages abbreviation goes within the jumbled letters
spread means the letters of large are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Struggling with the pages of a big newspaper spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a newspaper spread but signals the anagram GRALE; 'in' sets the pages inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to struggle or tussle at close quarters, a synonym of wrestle.

clue.text: Tune librarian arranged as patriotic anthem

indicators.note: arranged, as music is, signals the letters of the two words put in a new order

explanation.surface: A librarian sets a tune as a national song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of TUNE LIBRARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This rousing song celebrating Britain's naval might is a famous British patriotic anthem, sung at the Last Night of the Proms.

clue.text: Conservative featured in Panorama supporting a welfare payment for teens

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so it follows the earlier part

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

indicators.note: featured in means the letter goes inside the word for panorama

parts.note: a scene is a view or panorama

explanation.surface: A Tory appears on the BBC's Panorama backing benefits for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs programme, but here it just means a view; 'supporting' places it below in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence is the period of life between childhood and adulthood, roughly the teenage years.

clue.text: Pasta guzzled by misshapen Neapolitan

indicators.note: guzzled by means the word sits swallowed inside the words misshapen Neapolitan

explanation.surface: A deformed man from Naples wolfs down pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guzzled by' puts the answer inside misshaPEN NEapolitan.
explanation.definitionFit: Penne is a type of Italian pasta in short tubes cut at an angle.

clue.text: To gripe about act of self-aggrandisement

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of to gripe are rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining about something can be a way of puffing yourself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TO GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is activity undertaken mainly to boost one's own vanity or self-importance.

clue.text: Almost all spirits and wine vessels are secured thus

indicators.note: almost all means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: mood can mean one's spirits, as in high spirits
red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: Sailors with drink and wine aboard make sure their ships are tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' tempts as alcohol beside 'wine', but it means mood; 'Almost all' cuts its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats tied up to a buoy or quay are said to be fastened this way; the definition describes the state of the ships.

clue.text: Cats, for example, calm us, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that cats might soothe them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges CALM US I; 'Cats' is the Lloyd Webber show, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is a famous Andrew Lloyd Webber stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Prepare to drive in comfy seat

parts.note: to set something is to prepare it, as in set the table
to tee is to drive off from a golf tee

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready for a car trip while sitting in an armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a padded seat for two or more people.

clue.text: Article regarding tax returns for Greek restaurant

indicators.note: returns means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
re means regarding, as in a letter heading
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about tax returns filed by a Greek eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like tax forms but reverses AN RE VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek café or eatery serving local food and wine.

clue.text: Salvage short snooker implement and a different snooker implement

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the first implement is dropped

parts.note: a rest is a stick used in snooker to support the cue for long shots
a cue is the stick used to strike the ball in snooker

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves a broken rest and another cue from the snooker hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts REST to RES. Snooker is a British table game like pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue is to save from harm or loss, the same as salvage used as a verb.

clue.text: Choke, spitting out large rum

indicators.note: spitting out means the letter for large is expelled from the synonym

parts.note: to strangle is to choke
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone splutters on a big mouthful of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spitting out' removes L from STRANGLE. 'rum' is the adjective meaning odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Reportedly, what's found beneath a trunk road

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard when said

parts.note: a root lies underground below a tree trunk

explanation.surface: A rumour about what lies under a major highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk road' looks like one phrase for a main road, but 'trunk' belongs to the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or road taken from one place to another.

clue.text: I regularly avoid being taken in by county council regarding citizens

indicators.note: being taken in by means these letters go inside the council's abbreviation

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for county council, a British local authority

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word avoid

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to avoid being duped by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the even letters of 'avoid'; 'being taken in by' means duped on the surface but signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic is the adjective for matters of a town or of its people and their public duties.

clue.text: Chlorine's not right in girl

indicators.note: not means the following letters are excluded from the element's name

explanation.surface: A chemist notes a girl lacks chlorine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R and IN from CHLORINE; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is a girl's name, so it stands for a female given name.

clue.text: Speed setting for guided missile?

definitions.meaning: a car device holding a chosen speed without the pedal
a Cruise is a type of missile, and guiding it is controlling it; the question mark marks the whimsy

explanation.surface: A clue asking what speed one would set for a missile in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The car feature keeps a steady speed; read literally, the phrase is the steering of a Cruise missile.

clue.text: Chop top off smooth and shiny vegetable

indicators.note: chop top off means the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A cook trims the end of a glossy vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop top off' removes S from SLEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: A leek is an onion-family vegetable with a long white stem, Wales's national emblem.

clue.text: Calm broken by promo song

indicators.note: broken by means the first word is split open with the second placed inside

parts.note: serene means calm
an ad is a promotional piece, like a promo

explanation.surface: A peaceful moment is interrupted by a promotional jingle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' signals that the promo's abbreviation is placed inside the word for calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song, traditionally sung beneath a sweetheart's window.
